prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which enabled incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange my preferred configuration is unchanged: a single prize part on B022 for Holst, Drucker and Mojsov. The case rests on a specific discovery chain, not on the unanimous openings: Holst's human incretin physiology, Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, and Drucker's work on the biology of proglucagon-derived peptides and its translational rationale. The mechanism is mature, independently replicated in human physiology, and confirmed in large randomized outcome trials for glycaemia, body weight, and cardiovascular and renal endpoints. No member raised a maturity objection, and the discussion has not produced a reason to think a later year would improve the case. A two-part prize is not needed to make this one defensible. Keeping B022 as the sole part leaves the three-person ceiling intact for the physiological discoverers and keeps the citation anchored in what was discovered.
statement.case_against: Attribution is still the weak point and round 1 did not remove it. Habener sits outside the credited names, and Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is contested in the public record, which none of us can settle from the supplied evidence. Knudsen's peptide engineering of liraglutide and semaglutide is excluded by the three-person ceiling. I now weigh that exclusion more heavily than in round 1: Linnarsson is right that I should not treat it as a separate, naturally later recognition, because Nobel practice rarely offers a second chance. I accept it as a real cost and not as a technicality. I still prefer the discovery-centred configuration, because widening it to drug development would blur the citation and cut into the physiological core, but I hold that view knowing what it leaves out.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius objected to calling Mojsov's contribution merely contested, arguing that identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) form turned a physiological curiosity into a drug target, and that leaving her out would be harder to defend than leaving out an industrial developer.
responses.response: I accept this correction. In round 1 I described Mojsov's standing as contested without separating the existence of a priority dispute from the weight of her scientific contribution. The identification and synthesis of the active form is a distinct step that the later pharmacology depended on, and I cannot see how the citation could say what was discovered without it. That is why I keep her in the trio. I also agree with your wording point: the citation should name the physiology and the active peptide and should not read as a verdict on the later pharmacology, so I have kept that framing. The unresolved Habener question remains, and I cannot weigh it from the supplied evidence, so I record it as an uncertainty and not as a reason to change the names.

responses.point: Perlmann argues that Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer is a separate line from CAR engineering, prefers June and Sadelain for B003, and says the missing early chimeric-receptor concept (Eshhar) is a gap that counts against B003 this year.
responses.response: I agree on both points, and I now go further than in round 1. My opening trio merged two achievements, and the two-name version is the only one with a coherent citation. Your second point matters more to my ranking. If the original chimeric-receptor concept is outside the credited names, a June and Sadelain citation has to be worded around receptor design and costimulation for clinical use, and the committee would be choosing to leave the earliest concept uncredited. I still keep B003 as my first alternative because the patient benefit is demonstrated and durable, but I treat it as a strong alternative and not as a co-prize this year, since that attribution gap would then stand beside the Knudsen exclusion on the same ballot.

responses.point: Linnarsson qualifies my round-1 remark that Knudsen could be recognised separately, noting that Nobel practice rarely offers a second chance, so excluding her is a real cost.
responses.response: I agree and have changed my wording and my weighting of that point, though not my configuration. I should not have implied that her exclusion is neutral. My reason for still not crediting her is scientific and not a matter of convenience. Her contribution is peptide engineering that made weekly dosing and the obesity indication possible, which is a different achievement from the physiology that this citation names, and with a three-person ceiling I cannot add her without removing Holst, Drucker or Mojsov. I would rather state that cost openly than hide it in the allocation.

responses.point: Svenningsson says CAR-T could reasonably become a second prize part if GLP-1 is narrowed to two names, asks that this be discussed explicitly because it changes the three-person limit, and names B050 as the cleaner two-person fallback.
responses.response: I have considered this and do not propose a second part. With B022 at three names the ceiling leaves no room for any other person, and narrowing B022 to two would drop Mojsov, Holst or Drucker, each with a decisive claim. I would not weaken the strongest configuration to make space for an alternative. On your fallback, B050 has the cleanest attribution on the list, but its medical consequence is indirect, so I keep it as my second alternative behind B003.

uncertainties: Whether Habener's role in the proglucagon gene and the early peptide work should displace or accompany Mojsov in the credited names, which the supplied evidence cannot settle.
Whether the committee accepts that the Knudsen exclusion, which I now regard as a real cost, is justified by a discovery-centred citation.
Whether the missing chimeric-receptor originators (Eshhar and others) are a gap too large for any B003 configuration, which would affect how I use it as an alternative.
How to weigh the TOR conduct concerns raised in round 1, which I cannot assess from the supplied evidence.
statement.conflict_note: No documented conflict with any credited name on the shortlist. I have co-authored with Linnarsson and Frisen, neither of whom is a credited candidate, and I regard shared affiliation with Karolinska Institutet as not a conflict. I do not know of a relationship with Hall, Schreiber or Sabatini, and I cannot assess the conduct concerns raised about a TOR candidate.
